title: Accounts Administrator - URGENT
description:
Accounts Administrator- Fixed Term- Urgent Start

Location: Belfast
Job Type: Fixed-Term Contract (until 31 December 2026)
Hours: Full-Time
Salary: £26,000 - £28,000 per annum (depending on experience)
Start Date: Immediate

Apple Recruitment is delighted to be recruiting for an Accounts Administrator on behalf of a well-established organisation based in Belfast.

This is a Fixed Term Contract until 31st December 2026 with the possibility of extension.

This is an excellent opportunity for an organised and detail-oriented administrator to join a busy Accounts and Property Management team. The successful candidate will provide administrative and accounts support, assisting with invoice processing, maintaining accurate records, responding to enquiries and ensuring the efficient day-to-day operation of the
department.

The role would suit someone with previous experience in administration, accounts support, customer service or office administration who is looking to gain valuable experience within a professional and fast-paced environment.

The Role
The Accounts Administrator will support the Accounts and Property Management teams by processing information accurately, maintaining records, handling enquiries and assisting with general administrative duties.

This is a varied role requiring excellent organisation, strong attention to detail and a professional approach when dealing with clients, residents and contractors.

Key Responsibilities
- Accurately input invoice information into the company's ERP system.
- Respond to contractor enquiries by telephone and email, including invoice and account-related queries.
- Provide day-to-day administrative support to Account Managers and the wider team.
- Handle incoming calls from clients, residents and contractors in a professional and courteous manner.
- Process and maintain client information accurately and confidentially.
- Carry out general data entry, database maintenance, scanning, filing and document management duties.
- Escalate complex queries to the appropriate team members when required.
- Support the efficient operation of the Accounts and Property Management functions.
- Maintain accurate records and ensure information is up to date.

Essential Criteria
- Previous experience in an administrative, accounts administration, customer service or office support role.
- Excellent attention to detail and a high level of accuracy.
- Strong IT skills, including proficiency in Microsoft Outlook, Word and Excel.
- Professional telephone manner and excellent written communication skills.
- Ability to organise workload, prioritise tasks and meet deadlines.
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
- Reliable, professional and able to maintain confidentiality.

Desirable Criteria
- Experience using an ERP, finance, accounting or property management system.
- Previous experience processing invoices or providing accounts support.
- Experience within property management, housing, facilities management, construction or a related sector.
- Knowledge of residential property management administration.

Salary & Benefits
- £26,000 - £28,000 per annum (DOE)
- Fixed-term contract until 31 December 2026
- Immediate start available
- Opportunity to gain experience within a successful and professional organisation
- Varied role supporting accounts administration, customer service and operational delivery
- Supportive team environment
- Valuable experience within a busy office setting

Interested?
If you are an organised and proactive administrator with strong attention to detail and excellent customer service skills, we would love to hear from you.

To apply, please submit your CV to Patricia O'Neill at Apple Recruitment or contact us for a confidential discussion.

Apple Recruitment Services is acting as an Employment Agency in relation to this vacancy.
Apple Recruitment is an Equal Opportunities Employer and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified candidates.

title: Accounts Payable Assistant (12m FTC)
description:
We have an exciting opportunity for an Accounts Payable Assistant to join the Finance team, based in the A&O Shearman Belfast office.
Finance team - Belfast
Belfast finance is part of the A&O Shearman support services centre, which was founded in 2011 with the aim of offering support to the A&O Shearman network.
Within the Belfast finance team, our services encompass managing financial accounting and reporting, revenue and e-billing, credit control, accounts payable, and tax. We provide support to offices located in London, the United States, France, Luxembourg, Belgium, the Netherlands, and Germany. Our approach is marked by a robust dedication to client service, and we diligently adhere to service level agreements, targets, and deadlines to ensure that our performance aligns with client expectations.
What you will do
As a Finance Assistant in the Accounts Payable team, you will ensure high quality services are provided to both internal and external clients on a timely basis. You will also work with the Team Lead to continually strive to enhance the effectiveness and efficiency of the reporting systems and transactional processes, in addition to working with and supporting the appropriate Accounts Payable team to ensure accuracy and timeliness of work in accordance with pre-determined metrics.
- Ensure high-quality services are delivered to internal and external clients in a timely manner
- Collaborate with the team lead to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of reporting systems and transactional processes
- Support the accounts payable team to maintain accuracy and timeliness of work in line with pre-determined metrics
- Perform data entry tasks accurately and efficiently
- Handle client enquiries and provide appropriate resolutions
- Deliver detailed financial information as required
- Offer general support and advice to internal stakeholders
- Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives within the accounts payable function

What you will have
- Commitment to providing professional, responsive and effective relationships
- Excellent communicator and confident in interaction with others
- Delivers tasks in a professional and organised way with limited supervision
- Ability to work well under pressure and multitask to meet targets and tight deadlines, with a keen eye for accuracy
- Committed to the maintenance of established processes and systems
- Enthusiastic, proactive and flexible approach
- Ability to assimilate large amounts of information quickly & learn rapidly
- Experience of working within a busy accounts payable environment is advantageous

What we can offer you

title: Assistant Finance Officer
description:
Your new company
Hays are recruiting on behalf of a well-established public sector organisation based in Belfast. Due to ongoing organisational requirements, an opportunity has arisen for an experienced Assistant Finance Officer to join the team on a part-time basis. This is an excellent opportunity for a finance professional seeking flexible working arrangements within a collaborative and purpose-driven environment.

Your new role
You will provide vital support across a range of finance and administrative functions, helping to ensure the effective operation of financial systems, controls and reporting processes.

Key responsibilities will include:
- Supporting the finance function in accordance with established financial procedures and controls.
- Processing ad hoc payments and financial transactions.
- Assisting with month-end processes, including journal postings and preparation of management accounting information.
- Reconciling general ledger accounts and preparing financial reports and analysis as required.
- Supporting the preparation of year-end accounts, reconciliations and associated financial documentation.
- Assisting with procurement administration, maintaining records and supporting tendering activities.
- Providing information and supporting documentation for internal and external audit requirements.

What you'll need to succeed
- Accounting Technician Qualification is preferred.
- Experience preparing and maintaining nominal ledgers, including journal processing.
- Experience completing complex reconciliations and contributing to month-end reporting processes.
- Experience using a financial accounting system (Account NI desirable)
- Strong Microsoft Office skills, particularly Microsoft Excel.

What you'll get in return
- Competitive salary equivalent to £33,542 - £34,231 (pro rata).
- Part-time working arrangements of 14.8 hours per week across two days.
- Hybrid working model with a combination of office-based and remote working.
- Opportunity to gain valuable experience within a respected public sector organisation.
- Temporary contract until May 2027

What you need to do now
If you're interested in this role, click 'apply now' to forward an up-to-date copy of your CV, or call us now.
If this job isn't quite right for you, but you are looking for a new position, please contact us for a confidential discussion about your career.

Hays Specialist Recruitment Limited acts as an employment agency for permanent recruitment and employment business for the supply of temporary workers. By applying for this job you accept the T&C's, Privacy Policy and Disclaimers which can be found at hays.co.uk

title: Finance Officer
company: Independent Commission for Reconciliation and Information Recovery (ICRIR) - Agency - Permanent
advertiser_name: Independent Commission for Reconciliation and Information Recovery (ICRIR)
description:
Finance Officer

About The Role

We are recruiting a Finance Officer to be part of the Independent Commission for Reconciliation and Information Recovery (ICRIR) to deliver important workstreams that deliver on key objectives for the Commission. The role is a fast-paced and highly collaborative role, reporting to the Finance Manager. The successful candidate will be a driven, collaborative colleague, with good attention to detail, have experience of working to tight deadlines and will possess the ability and communication skills to build strong working relationships at all levels across the ICRIR and various stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

The main responsibilities of the role include, but are not limited to:
- Play a key role in the finance function by putting in place monthly controls to provide high-quality financial reporting and governance.
- Leading on transaction processing and being the finance contact for the Commission with the shared services provider.
- Processing monthly journals, purchase orders, receipts and invoices for payment.
- Monitoring and responding to queries in the Finance Team inbox
- Liaising with stakeholders including sponsor department (Northern Ireland Office), HM Treasury, Internal Audit and the National Audit Office.
- Supporting the year-end reporting, ensuring all audit requirements are met to enable the successful delivery of the year end accounts.
- Addressing audit recommendations and continuous improvement of financial processes and procedures.
- Prepare ad-hoc costings, budgetary and expenditure reports.
- Undertake any other relevant duties that may be required and are commensurate with the nature and grade of the post.

This list is not exhaustive, and the successful candidate will be required to carry out other duties within the scope of the post, as allocated by management.

We welcome the unique contribution diverse applicants bring and do not discriminate based on culture, ethnicity, race, nationality or national origin, age, sex, gender identity or expression, religion or belief, disability status, sexual orientation, educational or social background or any other factor. We are happy to discuss the role and answer any questions you may have. Please feel free to contact us for an informal conversation by emailing us at

Person Specification

Essential Criteria Qualifications

1. Successful completion of all examinations of the Association of Accounting Technicians (AAT) or the Institute of Accounting Technicians of Ireland (IATI) or an equivalent qualification.

Or

2. CCAB or equivalent part qualified accountant.

Experience and Skills
- 1 years' experience working in a finance function.
- Experience of a using computerised financial system.
- Proficient in using excel and other Microsoft Office packages.
- Ability to work as part of a team
- High degree of self-motivation and initiative.
- Demonstrate the values set out in the ICRIR code of Conduct
- Willingness and ability to be assessed against the requirements for CTC clearance, if not already cleared.
- Applicants must meet the nationality requirements for this role. Details of the nationality requirements can be found in the FAQs below.

Desirable Criteria
- Experience of the Account NI finance system
- Public sector finance experience

Salary Range: £31,000 - £34,692

Location Belfast

Our main operational base is in Belfast, with an operational site in London. Staff are split across both the London and Belfast Offices; therefore, you may be required to travel to London as well as maintain regular attendance in the office. You may also work from your home address, in line with the Commission's approach on hybrid working and with the agreement of your line manager.

Working Pattern Full time, part time and flexible working.

Contract Type This role is offered on a full-time permanent contract.

Security Level Willingness to be assessed against the requirements for, and ability to obtain, CTC clearance, if not already cleared.

Closing Date Monday 14th September .59pm

Interview Date Early October 2026

About Us

The Independent Commission for Reconciliation and Information Recovery is an independent organisation that has been established to recover information about Troubles/Conflict-related deaths and serious injuries to families, victims, and survivors and to promote reconciliation.

We are building a values-led organisation. We operate with integrity, impartiality, openness, accountability, and respect, as set out in our Code of Conduct. This is reflected in our fair and open recruitment processes. We encourage people to join us across all backgrounds, communities and faiths to help us deliver.

The Commission is based in Belfast, with further operational sites in Northern Ireland and London. Travel to all locations will be required, but hybrid working arrangements will help us support a range of flexible working patterns. This is an exciting opportunity to join an organisation with a unique and vital remit.

The Commission is formed of seven Commissioners, the Chief Commissioner, Sir Declan Morgan, the Chief Executive Officer, and the Commissioner for Investigations, as well as four Non-Executive Commissioners to provide challenge and scrutiny to the executive team.

We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. We welcome applications from all communities and backgrounds, including underrepresented groups. We value diversity in our workforce as it enhances our ability to serve the communities of Northern Ireland and the United Kingdom.

ICRIR's Code of Conduct

If you would have any queries or would like to contact us to discuss a reasonable adjustment, please email us at or call us on .
- Integrity
- Impartiality
- Openness
- Accountability
- Respect

For further information and to submit your application, click the apply icon.

title: Finance Administrator (Newtownards)
description:
Honeycomb are delighted to be working with the South Eastern Health and Social Care Trust to recruit a temporary Finance Administrator. This role will be based at Ards Hospital and offers £14.06 per hour.

The Company

This is an exciting opportunity to join the South Eastern Health and Social Care Trust and support an important finance project. The role will be based at Ards Hospital and will work closely with the Trust's finance team.

The Role

As a Finance Administrator, you will work alongside the finance team to support the implementation of a new finance system. You will work across the helpdesk function, assisting new users and responding to queries to ensure a smooth transition to the new system.

Key responsibilities:
- Providing financial systems support and troubleshooting
- Supporting colleagues and responding to user queries
- Assisting with the completion of Statutory Accounts
- Supporting financial governance, controls and audit requirements
- Identifying opportunities to improve processes and efficiency

The Person

The right person for this role will have a strong finance background combined with strong technical ability and experience working with computerised financial systems.

Essential Criteria:
- An HNC/D in a finance-related subject (or equivalent) plus relevant finance experience; or an NVQ Level 3 with appropriate experience; or two years' recent relevant experience at Band 3 or equivalent.
- Experience working with computerised financial systems in a busy finance office.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with experience working with a range of stakeholders.
- Good IT skills, particularly Microsoft Excel, and experience using financial systems.

Package and Benefits

This role offers an immediate start and a rate of £14.06 per hour. The position is temporary until the end of December.

To apply in confidence, please submit your CV via the link provided or contact Ashlea Parte for more information.

Please note: Successful candidates may need to complete a Basic or Enhanced Access NI check (fee of £18+). A previous conviction will not automatically prevent appointment; all disclosures are managed confidentially.

If you have a disability which means you require assistance at any stage of the recruitment process, please contact us directly to discuss. Honeycomb is committed to providing equality of opportunity to all.

Please note that we are currently receiving an exceptionally high volume of applications and will be unable to shortlist candidates who do not meet the specific requirements for this role. Due to this volume, we may be unable to provide individual feedback. We thank you in advance for your understanding.

title: Finance Officer
company: Your World Recruitment Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
Band 5 Finance Officer
Location: Newtownards / Hybrid working - 3 days in office, 2 at home
Job Type: Temporary
Duration of booking: Expected to last 3 months with possible extension
Proposed start date: ASAP
Pay Rates: Up to £15.88 per hour PAYE inclusive of holiday pay
Hours / Working Days: 37.5 hours per week / Monday to Friday, 9am - 5pm
Job Description
- To liaise with, and meet with senior Trust staff in order to assist with their understanding of budgets or to assist with any related queries.
- Assist with the annual budget setting process within agreed guidelines and timetables, and helping to ensure that they reflect the Trust's financial strategy and income profile.
- Assist the Band 7 Finance Officer in contributing to the development of cash releasing efficiency plans, recovery plans and contingency plans for the directorate.
- Support the Finance Manager in the early identification of threats to the financial stability of the Trust by highlighting risks within the directorate and agreeing rectification measures to ensure breakeven is achieved.
- To assist in developing the use of financial systems, reporting and enquiry tools and working methods to advance the quality and efficiency of Financial Management information.
- To deal with ad hoc reporting and enquiries as required by Senior Finance Managers and other senior Trust staff.

Criteria for Application:
- Hold a current drivers licence and is a car driver
- University degree and 2 years suitable relevant financial experience
- or, AAT/HND qualified and 2 years suitable relevant financial experience

or, Part Qualified with one of the CCAB recognised bodies and 1 years suitable relevant financial experience
or, 3 years suitable relevant financial experience at Band 4 level
- Excellent written and verbal communication with a range of stakeholders
- Competent at Microsoft Excel, ability to manipulate large volumes of data, wide range of functions and then provide analysis on this data
- Confident with accounting principles - accruals, prepayments etc.
- Ideally, experience in management accounts, investigating variances.
- Ability to manage workload to meet department deadlines
